component.name: Alatus
component.summary: ASUS Hardware Control Center for Linux

description.p: Alatus is a lightweight, native Linux control center for modern ASUS laptops (including Vivobook, Zenbook, ROG, TUF, and ProArt series). It allows you to tweak deep hardware settings that are usually only available on Windows, featuring dynamic capability detection and tri-state hardware awareness.
This is a community package and is not officially supported by ASUS.

ul.li: Battery Care: Set charging limits to prolong battery lifespan.
Fan Profiles: Switch between Quiet, Balanced, Performance, and Full Speed modes.
OLED Care: Manage flicker-free dimming and pixel refresh conditioning.
Keyboard Backlight: Single-zone RGB and desktop accent color sync.

description.p: Alatus 2.0.0 Major Architectural Refactor: Dynamic DeviceContext hardware layer, tri-state capability awareness across CLI and Slint UI, dynamic policy engine with AC debounce and battery hysteresis, startup state reconciliation, declarative multi-model device profile expansion, and characterization test suite.

Unified binary consolidation, modular architecture, keyboard RGB inactivity timeout policy (Never, Battery Only, Always), single-instance advisory lock, and multi-distro packaging automation (RPM/DEB).

Maintenance and hardening release: refreshed Alatus identity metadata, clarified event-driven session reconciliation, refined packaging integration, and added supply-chain verification for release artifacts.

Alatus v1.0.0 Genesis Release: Definitive initial stable release of the native ASUS hardware orchestration suite in Rust, featuring ACPI WMI DebugFS thermal management, Full Speed fan profile, ITE5570 LampArray RGB, Flicker-Free OLED Care, single-instance D-Bus desktop integration, and Material 3 Slint interface.
